Garden Maintenance in Guelph

Weeded, edged and tidy garden beds — kept that way all season, or reset in one visit.

Garden beds are where a property slips first. A few weeks of rain and sun, and weeds are seeding, groundcover is creeping into the lawn, and fallen branches are piling up behind the shrubs. We keep beds clean on a schedule that suits your garden, or reset an overgrown yard in one visit.

It’s the same local crew that mows Guelph lawns every week, so beds, edges and lawn are looked after together — one quote, one invoice, no contract.

The service

What garden maintenance covers

  • Bed weeding and cultivating, roots and all
  • Overgrown groundcover and climbing vines removed
  • Fallen branches and yard debris cleared
  • Bed edges re-cut so lawn and garden stay separate
  • Mulch top-ups where beds need it
  • Recurring visits through the season, or a one-time reset

Regular visits are what keep beds easy. A bed weeded every few weeks takes minutes; a bed left for a summer takes an afternoon and a lot more of the budget.

Local know-how

Why garden beds get away from you

The weeds you can see are only half of it. Goutweed (bishop’s weed), creeping bellflower and similar aggressive plants spread through underground runners, so pulling the tops just resets the clock. We dig out roots and runners, and we’re upfront that a heavily infested bed usually needs follow-up visits to catch regrowth.

Read more

Ontario restricts cosmetic pesticides, so bed weeding here is hands-on work. That suits a maintenance schedule: small, frequent visits beat one big fight in August. For the lawn side of weeds — thickening turf so weeds can’t establish — see weed control.

Branches and limbs. We clear fallen branches and limbs that can be handled safely from the ground. Anything large, or still attached high in a tree, is a job for a certified arborist — we’ll tell you when that’s the case.

Pricing

What affects the price of garden maintenance

Garden maintenance is quoted per property. The main factors:

  • Number and size of beds
  • How overgrown they are at the first visit
  • Visit frequency — recurring visits cost less per visit than a one-time reset
  • Mulch, if you want beds topped up
Common questions

Garden maintenance questions

How often should garden beds be maintained?

Through the growing season, every two to four weeks keeps most beds clean with little effort. Beds left longer need a bigger reset visit.

Can you remove groundcover like goutweed?

Yes. Aggressive groundcovers spread through underground runners, so we dig out the roots, not just the tops. Heavily infested beds usually need follow-up visits to catch regrowth, and we’ll be upfront about that.

Do you remove fallen branches?

Yes — fallen branches and limbs that can be handled safely from the ground. Large limbs, or anything still attached high in a tree, needs a certified arborist.

Is garden maintenance the same as weed control?

They overlap. Weed control covers lawn and beds using pesticide-free methods. Garden maintenance is the broader upkeep of your beds: weeding, groundcover and vine removal, debris, edges and mulch.

Can I book a one-time cleanup instead of a schedule?

Yes. A one-time reset is common before a sale, an event, or the start of the season. No contract either way.
